original_value: This paper proposes the q-sigmoid functions, which are variations of the sigmoid expressions and an analysis of their application to the process of enhancing regions of interest in digital images. These new functions are based on the non-extensive Tsallis statistics, arising in the field of statistical mechanics through the use of q-exponential functions. The potential of q-sigmoids for image processing is demonstrated in tasks of region enhancement in ultrasound images which are highly affected by speckle noise. Before demonstrating the results in real images, we study the asymptotic behavior of these functions and the effect of the obtained expressions when processing synthetic images. In both experiments, the q-sigmoids overcame the original sigmoid functions, as well as two other well-known methods for the enhancement of regions of interest: slicing and histogram equalization. These results show that q-sigmoids can be used as a preprocessing step in pipelines including segmentation as demonstrated for the Otsu algorithm and deep learning approaches for further feature extractions and analyses.

result.paraphrase: This paper introduces q-sigmoid functions, variants of sigmoid expressions, and examines how they can be used to enhance regions of interest in digital images. Built on the non-extensive Tsallis statistics from statistical mechanics via q-exponential functions, these new functions are evaluated for image-processing tasks, especially region enhancement in ultrasound images heavily affected by speckle noise. Before presenting results on real images, the authors analyze the asymptotic behavior of the functions and their effect on synthetic images. In both experiments, q-sigmoids outperformed the original sigmoid functions and two established region-enhancement methods, slicing and histogram equalization. The findings indicate that q-sigmoids can serve as a preprocessing step in pipelines that include segmentation, as shown with the Otsu algorithm and deep learning approaches for subsequent feature extraction and analysis.
